findings.title: Sync-mode schema uses computed keys from zod instances, so it never matches real token responses
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal key "ZodString", and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` to "ZodOptional". The minimum schema therefore requires a numeric property named "ZodString" and does not describe the token response at all. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, every refresh fails with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". The intended expiry-field check needs to be written differently (for example with z.record or a passthrough object).

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token string is written into stored credentials
findings.body: When the refreshed token response has no refresh_token, this assigns the literal string "refresh_token" to it. The caller then persists that value to the credential row. The next refresh will send "refresh_token" as the refresh token and fail, so the integration is silently broken. The original refresh token should be kept instead of a fake value.

findings.title: parseRefreshTokenResponse return value (SafeParse result) is stored as the credential key
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse wrapper `{ success, data }`, not the parsed data. Here that wrapper is assigned to `key` and saved with `data: { key }`. The stored Google credential becomes `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, so googleCredentialSchema.parse on the next construction fails. The code should use `.data` as the other callers do.

findings.title: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode, but the caller reads `.data`
findings.body: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the fetch Response. `res?.data` is undefined, so `token.access_token` on line 95 throws a TypeError, and the refresh fails. The same mismatch affects hubspot, zoho-bigin and zohocrm, which read `.data` or `.expiresIn` from a value that is a Response in sync mode.

findings.title: Sync-mode Response is treated as a token object, producing NaN expiry and an empty stored credential
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response when syncing. `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` is then undefined, so expiryDate becomes NaN. Line 198 then persists a Response object, which serializes to an empty object, as the credential key, and `setAccessToken(undefined)` is called on line 202. Hubspot tokens are lost after the first sync-mode refresh.

findings.title: Sync-mode Response is read through `.data`, which is undefined
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response in sync mode, so `tokenInfo.data` is undefined. `tokenInfo.data.error` on line 96 throws a TypeError, and the Bigin token refresh fails whenever credential sync is enabled.

findings.title: credentialId is passed where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens takes `userId: number | null` and sends it to the self-hoster endpoint as calcomUserId. Bigin passes `credentialId`, a credential row ID, so the sync endpoint receives the wrong user. The field should be the owning user's ID (credential.userId), as in the other integrations.

findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported
findings.body: getClient now calls `prisma.credential.update` (line 96), but the file has no import of prisma. Every SalesforceCalendarService construction throws a ReferenceError, which breaks all Salesforce calendar operations, not just sync-enabled setups.

findings.title: Salesforce token refresh runs on every client construction regardless of sync configuration
findings.body: The refresh call to login.salesforce.com and the credential write now run unconditionally in getClient. Previously the stored access token was used. Every service construction now hits the token endpoint and rewrites the credential, which adds latency and rate-limit pressure. It also bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, so self-hosters' sync endpoint is never used for Salesforce. The statusText === "OK" check is also unreliable, since HTTP/2 responses have no status text.

findings.title: Updating an existing credential does not clear the invalid flag
findings.body: When a credential was previously marked `invalid` (for example after invalid_grant), the sync update only replaces the key. The credential stays invalid even though fresh credentials were just synced, so the app remains unusable until the user reconnects manually.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with a non-constant-time string comparison
findings.body: The secret is compared with !==. A timing-safe comparison (for example crypto.timingSafeEqual over equal-length buffers) should be used for webhook authentication.

findings.title: Invalid request bodies cause an unhandled 500 instead of a 400
findings.body: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws a ZodError when the body is malformed. It is not caught, so the handler returns 500. JSON.parse of the decrypted keys on line 57 has the same problem for invalid ciphertext or non-JSON plaintext. Both should return 4xx with a clear message.

findings.title: Sync request to the external endpoint carries no authentication and no timeout
findings.body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends the user ID and app slug with no shared secret, auth header, or timeout. The self-hosted endpoint cannot verify that the caller is Cal.com, and a hung endpoint blocks the token refresh indefinitely. Its response is also not validated before being trusted.

findings.title: No tests added for the new webhook, sync refresh path, or encryption handling
findings.body: The PR adds a new authenticated write endpoint, a new refresh branch used by about 15 integrations, and new encryption logic, with no unit or integration tests. The PR checklist confirms this. The sync-mode bugs above (wrong return types, missing import, placeholder token) would have been caught by even basic tests of refreshOAuthTokens and parseRefreshTokenResponse.
